newsitem.title: USA: DCR Reaffirms TCI Communications rating.
newsitem.headline: DCR Reaffirms TCI Communications rating.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it has reaffirmed the ratings of TCI Communications Inc senior notes and debentures at double-B-plus, its senior subordinated notes and convertible subordinated debentures at double-B and its preferred stock at double-B-minus.
About $14.5 billion of outstanding debt is affected by the reaffirmation.
TCIC is the largest subsidiary of Tele-Communications Inc. TCIC is the largest operator of cable television systems in the U.S. with about 14 million subscribers.

TCIC has said that, going forward, it will put greater emphasis on investing money where appropriate returns can be achieved in a shorter time horizon. Therefore, TCIC's financial strategy will focus on creating free cash flow in 1997 with the intent to reduce leverage and increase financial flexibility, D&P said in a statement.

The company has shifted its capital resources to a newer alternative digital compression technology. This shift should result in substantially lower capital expenditure requirements. Capital expenditures were about $1.8 billion in 1996. TCIC will significantly reduce its 1997 capital expenditure program from 1996 levels, which should result in meaningful free cash flow, D&P said.
TCIC's commitment to improving financial flexibility should lead to strengthening credit quality for the company, D&P said. ((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8787))
